claims.claim: urllib3 can automatically retry idempotent requests.
claims.citation: urllib3 can automatically retry idempotent requests

claims.claim: The mechanism that retries requests in urllib3 also handles redirects.
claims.citation: This same mechanism also handles redirects

claims.claim: The number of retries in urllib3 can be controlled using the retries parameter of request().
claims.citation: You can control the retries using the retries parameter to request()

claims.claim: By default, urllib3 retries requests 3 times.
claims.citation: By default, urllib3 will retry requests 3 times and follow up to 3 redirects

claims.claim: By default, urllib3 follows up to 3 redirects.
claims.citation: By default, urllib3 will retry requests 3 times and follow up to 3 redirects

claims.claim: Specifying an integer for the retries parameter of request() changes the number of retries urllib3 performs.
claims.citation: To change the number of retries just specify an integer

claims.claim: Specifying retries=False for request() disables all retry and redirect logic in urllib3.
claims.citation: To disable all retry and redirect logic specify retries=False

claims.claim: Specifying redirect=False for request() disables redirects while keeping the retrying logic.
claims.citation: To disable redirects but keep the retrying logic, specify redirect=False

claims.claim: A Retry instance gives more granular control over retries in urllib3.
claims.citation: For more granular control you can use a Retry instance

claims.claim: A Retry instance can be configured for a total of 3 retries while limiting redirects to 2.
claims.citation: to do a total of 3 retries, but limit to only 2 redirects

claims.claim: urllib3 can be configured to disable exceptions for too many redirects and return the 302 response.
claims.citation: You can also disable exceptions for too many redirects and just return the 302 response

claims.claim: A retry policy can be specified at the PoolManager level.
claims.citation: you can specify the retry at the PoolManager level

claims.claim: A pool-level retry policy set on PoolManager can be overridden by specifying retries for request().
claims.citation: You can still override this pool-level retry policy by specifying retries to request()
